text:
oliver: hey folks, newbie question — running the quickstart and swapping my sandbox key for the hosted key causes a bunch of 429s. Is there a recommended local/dev flow for hosted keys?

tess: welcome! you should be able to call hosted directly but 429s often mean you're hitting concurrency/rlimits. what are you running (parallel streams or lots of short calls)?

oliver: mostly parallel streaming from a local harness (10 streams while iterating). sandbox seemed fine but hosted flips to 429s after a bit.

rahul: streaming uses up open-connection quotas. sandbox = very conservative by default; hosted is higher but still has caps per-account and per-route. for dev i: reduce parallel streams, reuse connections, or use the local proxy to replay responses.

oliver: local proxy — does that require different creds? i don't want to expose hosted keys in forks/CI.

tess: we use REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY for proxy recording and REDWOOD_PROXY_URL (http://localhost:8080). for PRs use sandbox or recorded responses. only run hosted calls on main with a short-lived hosted token.

rahul: snippet we use for GH Actions: ```yamlname: Integrationon: pull_request:jobs:test:runs-on: ubuntu-lateststeps:- name: Run tests  env: REDWOOD_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY }}  run: ./scripts/ci-run.sh```then on main branch replace env to REDWOOD_API_KEY secret. keep hosted secrets restricted.

oliver: perfect. if we need more sandbox quota for an onboarding demo, how do i request it?

devex: ping @devex in slack with the expected concurrency, rps, time window and justification. include team and jira/ticket if you have one. temporary boosts usually 1-2 business days. emergencies DM the devex lead.

proxy-bot: Tip: when recording with the proxy, scrub any sensitive user data and rotate sandbox tokens after sharing artifacts.

oliver: thanks all — i'll switch PR runs to proxy + sandbox, open a devex request for demo load, and avoid storing hosted keys in forks. :tada:
